messages:
mira: Heads up — proposing we change how trace-derived latency SLOs are measured. Right now our dashboard p50/p99 includes exporter/delivery time (the exporter child spans), which is inflating the tail during occasional buffering. I think the SLI should target in-service processing only (span.kind=server) and subtract exporter child spans. Thoughts? :thinking:

sven: How do you plan to reliably separate exporter overhead from app work? exporters sometimes appear as client spans in the same trace but not always named consistently.

alex: We can do this without 100% perfect names. two practical approaches: 1) rely on span.kind and instrumentation library (exporter libs often set library.name like "otlp-exporter"), or 2) subtract any child spans that match "exporter.*" or have attribute telemetry.exporter=true. Example SQL-like query (pseudo):

```
SELECT trace_id,
       (MAX(span_end) - MIN(span_start) - COALESCE(SUM(case when span_name LIKE 'exporter.%' then duration_ms else 0 end), 0)) AS app_ms
FROM spans
WHERE span_kind = 'server' AND service_name = 'api-frontend'
GROUP BY trace_id
```

Then compute SLI on app_ms.

jamie: I like the subtraction idea but worried about losing useful signals — exporter failures are still user visible for end-to-end latency. We should keep both: "app-processing SLI" (exclude exporter) and "end-to-end SLI" (include exporter). Use app-processing for most error budgets that tie to our service code; use end-to-end for ops alerts on downstream pipeline issues.

katie: Dashboard + rollout UX note: changing an SLI is essentially changing an SLO. We should show historical comparison and run a canary of the new SLI for 14 days before switching budgets. Also we need to add a clear note in the Console that says which spans were excluded so customers understand. :eyes:

mira: Agreed on both counts — will add two panels: app-processing p50/p95/p99 and end-to-end p50/p95/p99. Plan: create a telemetry PR with the query + tag excluded span rules, keep old SLI for 30 days in parallel, and add a console changelog entry.

alex: One implementation detail: exporter buffering often shows up as long-running client spans on the same host. If we subtract child spans we should also ignore overlapping async events where exporter work happens after server_end (e.g., background flush). For those, we should subtract any child spans regardless of timing, but annotate when exporter.start > server_end so we can decide whether to treat as asynchronous (maybe still count in end-to-end only).

ops-bot: alert: ingest-exporter buffer spikes detected in us-west-2 between 2026-03-02T09:10Z and 09:25Z, avg queue_time 420ms — correlated with higher end-to-end p99.

mira: Thanks for the alert — that's exactly the kind of event this change would hide from the app-processing SLI but keep visible in end-to-end. I'll add an annotation on affected dashboard windows.

jamie: Sampling caveat: our tail SLOs rely on kept traces (head-based sampling). If exporter overhead correlates with certain requests and those traces are sampled differently, the subtraction could bias the p99. We should run a short experiment with full-sampled traces for one hour of traffic to validate.

katie: Ops followup: can we add a small badge on the SLO panel that says "includes exporter" or "excludes exporter" and link to docs explaining the subtraction logic? UX wants minimal surprise.

mira: Will do. I'll open telemetry PR + console PR today. Work items: (1) query + rules for excluded spans, (2) retain old SLI in parallel for 30d, (3) dashboard panels + badges, (4) run 1h full-sample validation and post results.

alex: For the PR, include both the SQL and a compact DSL variant for our trace-aggregator. Also add a unit test that constructs traces with exporter child spans to assert subtraction behaves as expected.

mira: Good call. assigning myself to the telemetry PR, tagging @alex for review.

sven: SGTM. small nit: ensure timeseries rollups don't double-count when a trace has multiple exporter spans — use DISTINCT trace_id grouping or sum unique exporter durations per trace.

mira: Yep — will dedupe exporter spans per trace before subtracting.

ops-bot: deploy-bot: telemetry PR #342 landed to canary cluster (canary-telemetry).

mira: Nice — I'll monitor the canary dashboards and post a short writeup in #eng-platform after 24h.

jamie: Thanks, will check the results and validate against error budget burn rates.

katie: Thanks all. :thumbsup:
